harvard.name: Harvard College
harvard.blurb: The most selective school to transfer in the country, admitting only a select few each year.
overview: Harvard College maintains one of the nation's smallest and most selective transfer programs. In recent admission cycles, the university has typically admitted between 10 and 20 transfer students from applicant pools of roughly 1,300 to 1,600, resulting in an admit rate around 1%.

Harvard accepts transfer applications for fall enrollment only. Applicants submit materials by March 1, and admissions decisions are generally released in mid- to late May. Because so few students are admitted, successful applicants usually demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, a compelling reason to transfer, and a strong record of impact beyond the classroom.
lookingFor: Outstanding academic performance in a rigorous college curriculum, typically with grades near the top of the applicant's class
Evidence that transferring to Harvard is essential for the applicant's academic and intellectual goals, rather than simply seeking a more prestigious institution
Strong engagement outside the classroom through leadership, research, service, entrepreneurship, or other meaningful contributions
Positive academic and disciplinary standing at the current institution, supported by the required College Report
Thoughtful application essays that clearly explain the applicant's educational journey, reasons for transferring, and fit with Harvard's academic community
requirements: Common Application for Transfer, including Harvard's transfer supplement, due March 1
Official transcripts from all colleges attended, along with a final high school transcript
College Report completed by the applicant's current institution and an Academic Evaluation from college instructors
Standardized test scores are optional under Harvard's current testing policy, though applicants should verify the policy for their application year
Admission decisions released in mid- to late May for fall enrollment

caltech.name: California Institute of Technology
caltech.blurb: One of the smallest, most STEM-intensive transfer programs in the country — a handful of seats each year.
overview: Caltech's transfer program is tiny even by elite-school standards. Transfer applicants may apply for fall entry only. Applications are due February 1, and decisions are released by mid-April, with admitted students given until June 1 to decide. Applicants for the 2025–26 cycle onward are required to submit SAT or ACT scores, reversing Caltech's earlier test-optional policy.

overview: UF's transfer acceptance rate has held remarkably steady around 47% in recent cycles, a stark contrast to a freshman acceptance rate that has fallen below 25%. The university admits 2,000-3,000 qualified transfer applicants most years.

UF prioritizes applicants from the Florida College System, with roughly two-thirds of admitted transfers coming directly from a community college and about 72% having already completed an associate's degree. The university offers fall, spring, and summer transfer terms.
lookingFor: At least 60 credit hours completed (UF strongly prioritizes incoming juniors) with a minimum 2.0 overall GPA and 2.0 in the last institution attended
Completion of the required prerequisite coursework for the applicant's intended major and college
Demonstrated foreign language competency, typically via two years of high school coursework or equivalent
A single major declared on the application, since changing majors after transfer admission is extremely limited
Particularly strong preparation for competitive programs like Business Administration, Nursing, and Engineering
requirements: UF's online transfer application and $30 fee, submitted six to nine months before the intended term
Transcripts from every institution attended, regardless of credit earned
SAT/ACT with Writing scores required for freshman/sophomore-level transfers and certain certification programs
Foreign language proficiency documentation
Decisions released around June 15 for fall entry, November 15 for spring, and April 1 for summer, all on a rolling basis

university-of-washington.name: University of Washington
university-of-washington.blurb: A major public research university with a transfer rate that closely tracks its overall freshman acceptance rate.
overview: The University of Washington's transfer acceptance rate has run around 42% in the most recent confirmed cycle, closely tracking its roughly 42% overall freshman acceptance rate — an unusually consistent pattern compared to most selective research universities.

UW offers transfer admission across all four quarters, though most degree-seeking students apply for autumn quarter. Winter quarter is open to U.S. applicants only, and spring quarter is limited to specific engineering and computer science departments.
lookingFor: Completion of at least 40 quarter credit hours, or completion of the College Academic Distribution Requirements if fewer credits are complete
A minimum 2.5 GPA to be considered, though the competitive mid-50% range for admitted transfers has run from 3.24 to 3.85
Strong grades in the applicant's intended major's specific course requirements
A well-articulated statement addressing academic and career goals and how UW supports them
For out-of-state applicants, a notably stronger GPA — often 3.75 or better — to be competitive
requirements: UW's own transfer application, due February 15 for fall and summer quarter entry (other quarters have separate deadlines)
Official transcripts from every college attended
TOEFL or IELTS scores for international applicants
Coursework in UW's College Academic Distribution Requirements if fewer than 40 transferable credits are complete
Decisions released in a notification window between March 1 and March 15 for fall/summer applicants

tulane.name: Tulane University
tulane.blurb: A private research university that has become dramatically more transfer-friendly in the most recent cycle.
overview: Tulane's transfer acceptance rate has swung dramatically in recent years — from as low as 18% to over 60% in the most recent Common Data Set, which reported 510 of 849 transfer applicants admitted for a 60.1% rate.

Tulane offers both a priority and regular fall deadline, plus a separate spring deadline. The university welcomes more than 150 transfer students most years and strongly encourages applying by the priority deadline for faster review.
lookingFor: At least a 3.0 cumulative GPA, with coursework in English Composition, higher-level mathematics, and ideally a foreign language
Attendance at a regionally accredited institution and good standing at the most recent school
An optional-but-recommended 250-word essay on reasons for transferring to Tulane
A record of engagement outside the classroom that speaks to fit with Tulane's civic-minded campus culture
For applicants without an SAT/ACT score, additional context supporting academic readiness
requirements: Common Application, with a February 1 priority deadline or April 15 regular deadline for fall entry, and October 15 for spring entry
Official high school and college transcripts
A counselor recommendation (teacher recommendations optional but welcomed)
Test-optional; SAT or ACT may be submitted in place of TOEFL/IELTS for international applicants
Decisions released by March 15 for priority applicants, or by June 15 on a rolling basis for regular applicants

university-of-miami.name: University of Miami
university-of-miami.blurb: A private research university where the transfer rate runs more than double its increasingly selective freshman rate.
overview: The University of Miami admits transfer students at a notably higher rate than its increasingly selective freshman pool — recent cycles have generally landed between 40% and 53%, with roughly 1,000-1,500 transfer applicants admitted most years.

UM accepts transfer applicants for both fall and spring semesters, with applications continuing to be accepted until the transfer class is full even after the priority deadline. Certain programs, like the Frost School of Music and Theatre Arts BFA, have their own earlier deadlines and audition requirements.
lookingFor: A minimum 2.0 GPA to be eligible for review, though the average incoming transfer GPA runs closer to 3.4-3.5
For applicants with 24 or more transferable credits, an admissions decision based exclusively on college-level academic record
A required 650-word essay addressing reasons for wanting to transfer to UM
For Miami Herbert Business School applicants, a B or better in an approved college calculus course
A College Report from every U.S. postsecondary institution attended as a degree-seeking student
requirements: Common Application, with priority deadlines of April 1 for fall entry and November 1 for spring entry (applications accepted until the class fills)
Official transcripts from every college attended, plus a final high school transcript if fewer than 24 credits are complete
College Report and a required transfer essay
Test-optional for applicants with 30+ postsecondary credits; required below that threshold
Decisions released starting mid-April for fall priority applicants, or mid-November for spring priority applicants

reed.name: Reed College
reed.blurb: A distinctive, academically intense liberal arts college whose transfer rate runs somewhat below its freshman rate.
overview: Reed's transfer acceptance rate has generally run somewhat below its roughly 27-35% freshman acceptance rate, landing in the 15-23% range in recent estimates, with the college admitting around 50-60 transfer students each fall from a pool of 200-250 applicants.

Reed accepts transfer applicants for both fall and spring terms, with a non-binding priority deadline in early March and a later regular deadline for fall entry. Transferring in as a junior is notably harder given Reed's junior qualifying exam requirement.
lookingFor: Strong intellectual engagement and academic performance, reflecting Reed's rigorous, discussion-based curriculum
The 'Paideia Essay' writing supplement and one new academic evaluation from a college instructor
A Registrar's Report from the most recently attended college
Preparation to complete Humanities 110 or its equivalent unless transfer credit is granted
For junior-standing applicants, awareness that an additional semester may be needed before the junior qualifying exam
requirements: Common Application, with a March 1 priority deadline or May 1 regular deadline for fall entry
Official transcripts from every college attended, plus a final high school transcript
Registrar's Report and one new academic evaluation from a college instructor
Reed College Common Application Writing Supplement ('Paideia Essay')
Decisions typically released within up to eight weeks of a complete application
